This page translates the reviewed DHIS2–GESIS mapping-cleaning workflow into
successive targets. The stage boundaries separate source reads, reviewed
corrections, validation queries, and persistence so each decision remains
auditable while the execution becomes reproducible.

::: {.callout-warning title="Preserve reviewed decisions while modernizing"}

The transformations below preserve the reviewed mapping decisions from the
legacy workflow. Each assigned object is a pipeline target. Diagnostic chunks in the final check
are deliberately unassigned: they inspect completed targets without adding
check-only objects to the graph. The authoring render does not execute them.

:::

::: {.manual-prereq title="Retain The Reviewed Source Evidence"}

The original mapping CSV and the four manually reviewed workbooks or CSVs
must remain available with their provenance intact. Before optimizing a stage,
record its input schema, expected row-count change, join cardinality, and the
review decision represented by each correction.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Load The Mapping Tools"}

Load the packages used by the mapping transformations and their diagnostic
queries. Scientific execution still occurs through the targets graph.

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| include: false
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(assertr)
library(stringr)
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 1 — Read And Filter The Source Mapping"}

This stage reads the base mapping, and assigns names to the four UID levels.
It removes the year 2022 and Belalanda from the list.

Interestingly, this reads in the crosswalk file separately from the
previous stage. We have to keep an eye on that...

```{r}
s1_gesis_xwalk_filtered_df <- read.csv(s0_gesis_xwalk_raw_csv) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(region_uid = UID, 
         district_uid = `UID.1`,
         commune_uid = `UID.2`, 
         fs_uid = `UID.3`) |>
  filter(cAnnee != "2022" & code_fs != "Belalanda") %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34812)  
```


:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stages 2–3 — Correct GESIS Codes And Fill The Known UID"}

This stage loads the reviewed corrections, checks UID consistency for both the
old and corrected codes, applies the corrected GESIS code, and fills the known
UID for GESIS code `630151027`.

```{r}
#| format: file
# 2) bits out of range ------
# Some clinic GESIS codes have the type or public/private bits out of the expected range, 
# sometimes, those GESIS codes should be corrected 
s1_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx <- str_subset(s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr, "CSB1 CSB2 PUBLIC PRIVATE.xlsx")
```

```{r}
s1_gesis_code_corrections_df <- read_xlsx(s1_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx) |>
  filter(!is.na(`NEW CODE`) & `NEW CODE` != "NEW CODE") %>% 
  setNames(c("old_code", "correct_code", "uid", "name", "status", "note")) %>% 
  unique()
```

```{r}
# make the adjustment to the mapping file
s1_gesis_xwalk_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_filtered_df %>%
  left_join(s1_gesis_code_corrections_df %>% select(code_fs = old_code, correct_code),
            by = c("code_fs")) %>% 
  mutate(code_fs = ifelse(is.na(correct_code), code_fs, correct_code)) %>% 
  select(-correct_code) %>%
  #manually fill the UID from other years for 630151027
  mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(code_fs == "630151027" & grepl("Ankilivalo", FS), 
                         "ZX5EkF6eC0x", 
                         fs_uid)) 

```


:::


::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 4 — Fill Missing UIDs From The Reviewed Workbook"}

This stage imports reviewed UID fills and applies them by GESIS clinic code.

```{r}
#| format: file
# 4) fill in missing UIDs for GESIS-years in mapping ----
# for GESIS-years for public clinics in the mapping file
# reporting data in 2018/2019 using this file for those 4 clinics 
s1_gesis_uid_fills_raw_xlsx <- str_subset(s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr, "gesis_missing_uid_in_mapping.xlsx")
```

```{r}
s1_gesis_uid_fills_df <- read_xlsx(s1_gesis_uid_fills_raw_xlsx) %>%
  mutate(code_fs = as.character(code_fs))

```

Join the reviewed fills onto the corrected mapping; leave unrelated UIDs
unchanged.

```{r}
s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_filled_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_corrected_df %>%
  left_join(s1_gesis_uid_fills_df %>% select(code_fs, uid),
            by = "code_fs") %>% 
  mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(is.na(uid), fs_uid, uid))  %>% 
  select(-uid)
# no GESIS changes, so only concern for this change is if there are other clinics 
# with the same UID --> only one of the UIDs filled in is otherwise in the 
# mapping file, and it appears to be the same clinics in the mapping 
# in the diagnosis dataset, there's a clinic in that same commune that has data 
# for earlier years that seems like its the same "Antanisoa", but it was private
# BUT the GESIS code for that clinic 120143040 also has another name "CMC Ambararata Est", 
# which seems to correspond to when the commune changes for that clinic 
# this clinic was not captured in our 21 GESIS - UIDs with concerning name changes 
# because it was private over that time span
```

The target retains the narrative evidence associated with these reviewed
exceptions next to the transformation.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 5 — Reconcile UID-Years With Multiple GESIS Codes"}

This stage classifies reviewer notes, retains the original internal diagnostic
as an executable check, evaluates external GESIS–UID consequences, and applies
deletions and renames.

The selected ZIP member is `VERIFIER fs_uid_year_with_multiple_gesis.csv`
and is comma-delimited, as read by the legacy script. The former Drive
underscore filename and semicolon dialect are outside this freeze.

```{r}
#| format: file
# 5) UID-years with multiple GESIS codes ---- 
s1_gesis_multiple_codes_raw_csv <- str_subset(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "VERIFIER fs_uid_year_with_multiple_gesis\\.csv$"
)
```

```{r}
s1_gesis_multiple_codes_reviewed_df <- read_csv(s1_gesis_multiple_codes_raw_csv) %>%
  mutate(change = case_when(grepl("the clinic was moved to the district of mandoto", note) ~ "keep", 
                            note %in% c("Same clinic", "OK", "ok") ~ "keep", 
                            grepl("^rename", note) ~ "rename", 
                            grepl("delete|Delete", note) ~ "delete",
                            TRUE ~ as.character(NA)), 
         code_fs = as.character(code_fs)) 
# started with 36 UID-years with multiple GESIS 
# there are 2 deletions, 16 renames, and 18 cases where its just two codes for the same clinic
# --> 18 UID-years with multiple GESIS at the end
```

```{r}
# make the change 
s1_gesis_xwalk_multiple_codes_reconciled_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_filled_df %>%
  # the UIDs got dropped when we rename, which only matters in one case 
  # whe the row needs to be deleted, so separately add in the delete cases vs rest
  left_join(s1_gesis_multiple_codes_reviewed_df %>%
              filter(change == "delete") %>% 
              select(cAnnee, code_fs, fs_uid, change),
            by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs", "fs_uid")) %>%
  filter(change != "delete" | is.na(change)) %>% 
  select(-change) %>% 
  left_join(s1_gesis_multiple_codes_reviewed_df %>%
              filter(change != "delete") %>% 
              select(cAnnee, code_fs, change,
                     fs_uid_correct = UID,
                     fs_name_correct = `NAME CLINICS`),
            by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs")) %>%
  mutate(fs_uid = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_uid_correct == "No UID" ~ "",
                            change == "rename" ~ fs_uid_correct,
                            TRUE ~ fs_uid),
         FS = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_name_correct != "" ~ fs_name_correct, 
                        TRUE ~ FS)) %>%
  select(-(change:fs_name_correct)) %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34810)
# deletes 2 rows, so now down to 34810 
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 6 — Add Reviewed GESIS Codes Missing From The Mapping"}

This stage constructs the accepted missing clinic across eight mapping years
and appends those rows.

A breaking change that must be noted: we aren't sure if the following
adds 8 rows, or adds row index 8...

```{r}
#| format: file
# 6) 10 GESIS codes not in the mapping ----
# 8 need to be deleted from diagnosis data, 1 doesn't have a UID, lets add row for the last 1
s1_gesis_uid_additions_raw_csv <- str_subset(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "VERIFIER clinic_codes_in_gesis_but_not_in_mapping.csv"
)
```

```{r}
s1_gesis_uid_additions_expanded_df <- read_csv(s1_gesis_uid_additions_raw_csv) %>%
  #filter(NOTE != "DELETE" & uid != "NO UID") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(uid) & str_to_lower(uid) != "no uid") %>%
  cross_join(
    tibble(cAnnee = c("2013", "2015", "OLD GESIS 2015", 
                      "NEW GESIS 2015", "2016", "2017", "2018", "2019"))
  ) %>% 
  transmute(cAnnee, 
            code_reg = NA_integer_, 
            region_uid = NA_character_, 
            region = NA_character_, 
            code_dist = NA_integer_, 
            district_uid = NA_character_, 
            district = NA_character_, 
            code_commune = NA_integer_, 
            commune_uid = NA_character_, 
            commune = NA_character_, 
            code_fs = as.character(clinic_code), 
            fs_uid = as.character(uid), 
            TYPE = str_split_fixed(name, " ", 2)[,1],
            FS = as.character(name)) 

```

Append those reviewed year records to the reconciled mapping.

```{r}
s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_added_df <- bind_rows(
  s1_gesis_xwalk_multiple_codes_reconciled_df,
  s1_gesis_uid_additions_expanded_df
) %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34818)
# adds 8 rows --> 34818  # this is incorrect, it should add row 8
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 7a — Apply Reviewed Code Substitutions"}

This stage contains the remaining UID- and year-specific substitutions,
deletions, and additions discovered while integrating the mapping with the
diagnosis data.

```{r}
# 7) some manual changes ---- 
# integrating the mapping with the diagnosis dataset identified these problems with the mapping file
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_codes_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_added_df %>%
  mutate(
    code_fs = case_when(
      fs_uid == "naW8NwTF6iT" & cAnnee == "NEW GESIS 2015"                                   ~ "430351007",
      fs_uid == "C43g5TA5l3j" & grepl("2015", cAnnee)                                        ~ "430351006",
      fs_uid == "hVmE01gCHfg" & cAnnee %in% c(2013:2019, "NEW GESIS 2015", "OLD GESIS 2015") ~ "220441038",
      fs_uid == "i9IyexSemHX"                                                                ~ "220441034",
      fs_uid == "xWIEcSCmwUF" & cAnnee == "2010"                                             ~ "440551024",
      fs_uid == "QxMf9Q2KYxI" & cAnnee == "2010"                                             ~ "440541010",
      TRUE                                                                                   ~ code_fs
    )
  )
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 7b — Replace The Disputed New-2015 Match"}

Replace the reviewed GESIS/UID pairing for new-2015 with the corresponding
old-2015 clinic record. Keep the source row as the evidence for its attributes.

```{r}
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_2015_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_codes_corrected_df %>%
  # replace what 340141015 is mapping to in new 2015, easier to delete one row and add another
  {
    rows_to_keep <- filter(
      .,
      !(fs_uid == "H9S6IOY4CKL" &
          code_fs == "340141015" &
          cAnnee == "NEW GESIS 2015")
    )

    replacement_row <- filter(
      .,
      fs_uid == "SnRMbMj7ON9" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015"
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        cAnnee = "NEW GESIS 2015",
        code_fs = "340141015"
      )

    bind_rows(rows_to_keep, replacement_row)
  }
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 7c — Replace The Historical Match"}

Construct replacement rows for 2011 through old-2015 from the reviewed 2016
record. The replacement years remain explicit so the affected coverage can
be inspected in the checks.

```{r}
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_historical_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_2015_corrected_df %>%
  # similarly, replace what 520551034 is mapping to in 2011 - old 2015
  {
    replacement_years <- tibble(
      cAnnee = c(2011:2014, "OLD GESIS 2015")
    )

    rows_to_keep <- filter(
      .,
      !(fs_uid == "JnmokyKVSvS" &
          code_fs == "520551034" &
          cAnnee %in% replacement_years$cAnnee)
    )

    replacement_rows <- filter(
      .,
      fs_uid == "d0n2W7psb6s" & cAnnee == "2016"
    ) %>%
      mutate(code_fs = "520551034") %>%
      select(-cAnnee) %>%
      cross_join(replacement_years)

    bind_rows(rows_to_keep, replacement_rows)
  }
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Stage 7d — Add The Reviewed New-2015 Record"}

Copy the accepted old-2015 record into new-2015 and assign its reviewed code.
Then apply the final UID/year deletions to produce the cleaned mapping.

```{r}
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_uid_added_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_historical_corrected_df %>%
  # add row for "H9S6IOY4CKL" in new 2015  
  {
    existing_rows <- .

    additional_row <- filter(
      .,
      fs_uid == "H9S6IOY4CKL" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015"
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        cAnnee = "NEW GESIS 2015",
        code_fs = "340141014"
      )

    bind_rows(existing_rows, additional_row)
  }
```

The final target removes the three excluded UID-years and retains the
reviewed row-count assertion.

```{r}
s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_uid_added_df %>%
  # drop rows for UID noCoZFMcMVa in 2010, 2011, old 2015
  filter(!(fs_uid == "noCoZFMcMVa" & cAnnee %in% c(2010, 2011, "OLD GESIS 2015"))) %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34816)
  # nrow # reduces from 34819 to 34816 rows
```

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Compare Most Recent Archived Data And Target Facility Mappings"}

**Review note (2026-11-08).** The researcher reports that the initial
shape checks on pages 18–21 appear to pass. This records the initial facility-mapping shape review.
This is a researcher-reported observation from the interactive review,
not an independently rerun acceptance test. It does not establish
key-level equality, measurement-value parity, or unchanged diagnosis
definitions/IDs. Retain any remaining discrepancies for review.

Run these chunks in order from the repository root after the targets build.
These are exploratory summaries; interpretation is left to the reader.
[Most recent archived data baseline](mapping/legacy-pipeline-map.qmd#most-recent-archived-data-comparison-baseline)
records the selected iterations, evidence, and provenance limits. The shared
selection is versioned in `src/archived-comparison-baseline.R`.

Use the May 1, 2025 script-1 intermediate: the most recent archived data
found for this stage.

Load the pair for this page. Braces keep these session assignments out of
`tar_tangle()`; the objects remain available for interactive exploration.

```{r}
{
  archived_baseline <- dget(here::here("src", "archived-comparison-baseline.R"))
  legacy_zip <- here::here(archived_baseline$archive_zip)
  old_mapping <- read.csv(unz(
    legacy_zip, archived_baseline$facility_mapping_member
  ), check.names = FALSE)
  new_mapping <- targets::tar_read(s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df)
}
```

**Rows and columns.**

```{r}
tibble::tibble(
  source = c("most recent archived data", "current pipeline"),
  rows = c(nrow(old_mapping), nrow(new_mapping)),
  columns = c(ncol(old_mapping), ncol(new_mapping))
)
```

**Column names and order.**

```{r}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_len(ncol(old_mapping)), column = names(old_mapping)),
  `current pipeline` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_len(ncol(new_mapping)), column = names(new_mapping)),
  .id = "source"
)
```

**UID coverage by year, including blank or missing UIDs.**

```{r}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = old_mapping |> dplyr::summarise(
    rows = dplyr::n(), uids = dplyr::n_distinct(fs_uid, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_uids = sum(is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == ""), .by = cAnnee
  ),
  `current pipeline` = new_mapping |> dplyr::summarise(
    rows = dplyr::n(), uids = dplyr::n_distinct(fs_uid, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_uids = sum(is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == ""), .by = cAnnee
  ),
  .id = "source"
)
```

:::
